ratings_why.fun: The T4-T6 ambush chains are a great board puzzle, but Tiers 1-2 barely win fights, and Patient growth only comes on wins, so the curve stalls when you most need it.
ratings_why.distinct: Units hidden in their own slot, set off by a neighbour dying, with the preview showing closed Lids, plays unlike any of today's tribes. The split between Springing and waiting gives it two real builds.

verdict_why: The Spring rules need one fix so chain cards can't loop, and the early tiers could use a body that wins fights.

points.text: Lurk never says a unit that is already up can't Spring again. Two Lurkers side by side with Signal-Thread Spinner would set each other off forever. Say that only a Lurker under its Lid can Spring.
An Inner Guard given Lurk, with the Past Master out, makes 'your leftmost Lurker' unclear: it could pick itself or a Lurker that is already up. Make it 'your leftmost other Lurker under a Lid'.
Tapwell does nothing in a Tier 1 fight unless a Money Spider dies beside it. A small Spring effect, or a Lurk card at Tier 2 that is a strong fighter, would carry the early rounds.
Patient growth only comes on wins, so a losing streak stops it. A card that rewards Lurkers that Sprang in a lost fight would give the Lodge a way back.

standouts.why: It turns a hidden Lurker into a counter-attack against the enemy's swing. It's the clearest 'trapdoor' moment in the tribe.
Closing the Lids again doubles every knock synergy, and you have to place things carefully to get it.
A good Tier 4 multiplier that only works next to it, which makes the gaps on the board matter.

weakest.why: A 1/3 that sits out most early fights, at the tier that should win them.
A 2/5 whose only job is to pop one Lurker. It's thin at Tier 3.
It's below a body, and giving Lurk early often takes your best fighter out of the fight.

flags.note: As written, two Lurkers that Spring each other may never stop. See p1.
Its target with Lurk and the Past Master is unclear. See p2.
The Master repeating Pardo's and Mother's summons, with a golden Diadem and Corkhinge, can fill the board and make many Spring attacks. Slots cap it, but it needs a sim.
Mabyn makes every Lurker Patient, so Reader, Tapwell, Clerk and her own +3/+3 all fire every turn. A golden Mabyn with a golden Reader grows fast, but only by fixed amounts each turn.
On an all-Lurker board everything Springs at Start of Combat, giving seven double-damage Cleave hits before the enemy can act.
